items.sentence_en: The joke about the chicken crossing the road to get to the other side is an example of "anti-humor": meant to be funny because, on the surface, it is not.

items.phonetic: ðə ʤoʊk əˈbaʊt ðə ˈʧɪkən ˈkrɔsɪŋ ðə roʊd tɪ gɪt tɪ ðə ˈəðər saɪd ɪz ən ɪgˈzæmpəl əv "anti-humor*": mɛnt tɪ bi ˈfəni bɪˈkəz, ɔn ðə ˈsərfəs, ɪt ɪz nɑt.

items.sentence_en: Part of why corn syrup is in everything is because massive corn monocultures have created a surplus that agriculture companies are scrambling to get rid of.

items.sentence_en: Will we accept an economy where only a few of us do spectacularly well? Or will we build an economy where everyone who works hard has a chance to get ahead?

items.sentence_en: That man has hit bottom: his wife has left him, he's lost his job, and he's an alcoholic. The worst is that I know him--he used to be my boss five years ago.

items.sentence_en: And the good news is that today the economy is growing again. Wages, incomes, home values and retirement accounts are all rising again. Poverty is falling again.
